evidence.C1: In-game prompts like 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' and 'Follow the beach road' guide the player seamlessly from title to job completion without ambiguity.
evidence.C2: Distinct districts (Sol Beach, Rustport) and day/night cycles create mood, though the low-poly asset style is consistent rather than uniquely recognizable.
evidence.C3: Systems feed each other: 'cab passenger will not get in while you are wanted' and 'Tune-up shop pulls its shutters down' create interlocking consequences.
evidence.C4: Gate G8 passed for overlaps, but the mobile HUD (Screenshot 12) is dense with buttons that may obstruct the view during high-speed driving.
evidence.C5: Fact sheet explicitly states 'No one else has played any version' and details untested areas like 'How the driving feels to a person', demonstrating extreme honesty.

fixes: Conduct external playtesting: The fact sheet admits 'No one else has played any version' and the owner previously found it 'not fun enough', which is a critical risk to C3 (fun/variety) and C1 (stranger experience).
Simplify Mobile HUD: Screenshot 12 shows over 10 touch buttons overlaying the gameplay area, potentially obstructing vision and violating the 'reads at a glance' anchor for C4.
Reduce Title Screen Density: Screenshot 1 displays a dense 'How to play' list; simplifying this ensures the 'first screen' part of C1 is as accessible as the in-game prompts.

evidence.C1: Title screen lists keys needed first; first view shows red car and 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' with JOB 40 m beam visible; learner phase prevents early arrest; first job is short and ends at the Sol Wheel landmark.
evidence.C2: Four districts with distinct palettes (aqua/coral Meridian, pastel Sol Beach, rust/ochre Rustport), neon trim, lit windows at night, Sol Wheel with lights, Coastliner airship, sunset skies; day and night clearly differ.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs, six odd job types (Rush Order, Repo Run, Block Dash, Hot Parcel, Paper Round, Shadow Run), cab fares, property, 1-5 star police, 15 hidden packages, 12 stunt ramps, nitro, barrels, Tune-up shop, Sol Wheel ride, harbor courier - all feeding through perks.
evidence.C4: HUD reduced to cash and health; stars only when wanted; weapon line only 5s; clock moved to map/pause; pause screen is three buttons plus settings/perks; G8 passes at three resolutions; phone HUD adapts to top edge.
evidence.C5: Own names throughout; title screen states 'An original game with its own city, names and art, not affiliated with Rockstar, Grand Theft Auto or GTA V'; sheet plainly states driving feel unmeasured, radio unlistened to, no real phone tested, only one person has played it.

fixes: Get more than one human to playtest the game - the sheet admits 'One person has played it: the owner' and 'No one else has played any version', which leaves difficulty, fun, and pacing untested.
Have a human actually listen to the three radio stations - the sheet notes 'nobody has listened to it: whether the music is pleasant is not known' despite 13/14 automated checks passing.
Test touch controls on a real phone or tablet - the sheet states 'No real phone or tablet has run the game yet, so thumb reach, heat and frame rate on a phone are not known'.

evidence.C1: First view shows 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' with 'JOB 40 m' and the car in view; 'the first job is shorter and ends at a landmark'; learner phase means 'crimes bring no stars' and the car 'cannot be wrecked'; job 1 done by keys 'in 27.7 to 29.2 s'. Only flaw: 'Harbor courier shift ↵' sits beside New Game, so a stray Enter starts a timed shift before any onboarding.
evidence.C2: 'Day and night cycle with lit windows and shop fronts... neon trim', '86 painted walls', the Sol Wheel dusk shot is distinctive. But screenshot 5 shows plain grey facades and flat road at dusk — the district palettes ('aqua, coral, cream and lilac') do not read in every view, so 'recognisable from one screenshot' is not met everywhere.
evidence.C3: 'Six story jobs', odd jobs 'in six kinds taken in turn', cab fares, property, 15 packages, ramps, barrels, nitro; 'Perks (release 1.2) tie the side activities together' and 'Police heat now reaches the other systems'. Held off 10 by the sheet's own words: 'The sums are first guesses, not tuned by play', and no human has judged 2.0+ (owner's last verdicts: 'not fun enough', 'not good enough').
evidence.C4: 'the HUD is cash and health; the stars appear only when you are wanted', G8 'no overlaps at 3 sizes', pause is 'three buttons, settings and perks'. Nitpick: a wordy tutorial paragraph ('Near misses pay cash, and so does a slide. [Space] with the handbrake...') sits on screen while driving at 122 km/h, and job line + trick card + hint can stack at once.
evidence.C5: 'Own city, names and art' with the one allowed 'not affiliated' line (G9 pass). Limits stated plainly and unfavourably: 'No real phone or tablet has run the game yet', 'One person has played it: the owner... not fun enough', and the gate flake 'Once nine of ten passed: G3 failed... It was not seen again.' Nothing meaningful left to improve.

fixes: Get a real person to play 2.1 and tune the numbers by play: the sheet admits 'The sums are first guesses, not tuned by play', the owner's last verdicts on 1.8/1.9 were negative, and every lost Heat Wave try still ends with the player 'shot dead on foot within seconds'.
Gate the title-screen 'Harbor courier shift ↵' behind the first job (or remove the Enter shortcut) so a stranger pressing Enter cannot start a timed three-stop shift before any onboarding.

Lift the weakest views to the standard of the Sol Wheel dusk shot: screenshot 5's plain grey facades show the painted-wall and district-palette work does not read everywhere, which is what keeps C2 from the one-screenshot anchor.
